direction.comments: The macroscale is what you would expect from a Marvel Spider-Man action movie, though they try a few more stylistic choices to make it feel like a comic book movie that feel a bit tacky; while I wasn't too big of a fan of the new fight choreography, I cannot deny that the action sequences were entertaining and fun to watch; the microscale is surprisingly pretty good for a Marvel movie as Peter Parker acts like a spider in the middle of a web, serving as the center of interactions connecting old and new relationships; this movie is very much a more grounded MCU movie as it is about Peter Parker coming to terms with his depression and loneliness after the events of the last movie; storytelling is pretty standard for Marvel, taking a lot from Thunderbolts with how it uses emotion, empathy towards the protagonist's struggles, and character relationships to move the story forward; tension uses your emotional connection to the characters, and while the ending builds pretty good tension, knowing this is the first movie of a new trilogy gives the characters plot armor so you don't feel super uneasy or tense

performance.comments: Does a great job capturing Peter Parker's grounded, lonely, and depressed nature while building a web of relationships between his former friends and new companions, acting as the center of all the relationships in this movie
Given less material to work with this time around, but delivers a good performance and shares great real-life chemistry with Holland
A major standout in the movie who brings her character to life with great presence, sharing a strong dynamic with Holland and proving she can shine beyond Stranger Things
The CEO has done it again, serving as comic relief and doing a good job with his limited screen time, maintaining good chemistry with Holland that highlights their former friendship
One of the best performances in the movie, portraying a hardened, tough-guy anti-hero as The Punisher and sharing electric chemistry with Holland
Plays a pretty generic character as he is not really given that much material to work with; kinda just bland and monotonous as he gets the job done

Is kind of just thrown into this movie as he uses his past experience playing the character as the real driving force for this performance, making this ultimately feel like a "fulfilling his MCU contract" type of performance

cast.comments: Solid ensemble performance that thrives on strong chemistry, successfully building a web of relationships connecting Peter's past and present

story.comments: The concept is interesting and deals with Peter Parker's loneliness as he watches the world move on without being able to be part of his old past or connect with his old friends after No Way Home; the plot structure is a linear story that feels very much like a copy-cat of Thunderbolts in how the main character suffers from depression, the antagonist is framed as a misunderstood superhero with the government as the true threat, and they end up befriending them; character writing is surprisingly pretty good, painting Peter as more depressed and showing how distant Ned and MJ now feel, while giving the Punisher and the antagonist more empathy and humanity; the strength of the relationships also strengthens the character writing as it creates the web that centers around Peter Parker

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is pretty standard Marvel dialogue, being the playful and friendly tone you would expect from a Spider-Man movie; the humor is standard Marvel and Spider-Man humor, with a decent hit rate; the symbolism is decently strong, exploring concepts of loneliness, duty, and depression as Peter Parker feels isolated in a world without his former friends; while I did enjoy the symbolism for this movie, it is very similar to Thunderbolts; the foreshadowing is standard for Marvel, though it makes the ending feel a bit predictable

score.comments: Continues what was left off in the previous films, serving primarily for character building, tension, and tone without overshadowing the movie or providing memorable new themes

soundtrack.comments: Typical high-budget Marvel blockbuster needle drops; while the Tame Impala needle drop was okay, the Bad Bunny needle drop was terribly mixed into the scene, cutting off awkwardly and feeling very forced

cinematography.comments: Felt tacky and poorly executed, trying to be innovative with a comic book feel and motion shots that didn't land; additionally, the blue color palette felt very dull and it was overly obvious the movie was framed for ScreenX, making the aspect ratio and composition feel off; after you get used to the cinematography in the first hour, it is not so bad in the second half

editing.comments: Tries too hard to turn this into a comic book movie, feeling very on-the-nose and a bit tacky alongside the cinematography choices

sound.comments: Pretty strong sound design, delivering what you expect from a high-budget Marvel action movie

visual_effects.comments: Standard high-budget Marvel visual effects where nothing really blows you away; it feels a little too much at times, but looks good overall with some places better than others

production_design.comments: Captures New York fine, though it feels like a lot of it was shot on sound stages and interior sets rather than on-location in real New York

makeup.comments: Does a pretty good job, particularly showing the bruising Peter Parker and The Punisher get throughout his fights

costumes.comments: Good costume design; Spider-Man's suit is kept clean and un-overcomplicated, feeling reminiscent of Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield's suits rather than overly techy, and the Punisher gets a good suit as well

review.pacing: Pacing was pretty good for the most part; even at 2 hours and 25 minutes, it feels like a fun time that moves along just right
review.climax: Well-executed and gives great closure to many of the characters, even if it is pretty predictable
review.tone: Tonally it is a grounded Spider-Man Marvel movie, taking on darker and deeper themes of depression and loneliness similar to Thunderbolts; despite its more grounded feeling, this movie does feel like a playful Spider-Man movie you would expect from the MCU
review.final_notes: The product placement in the first hour is egregious (Little Caesars, BMW, Bero, Takis, etc.)
review.overall: Overall, 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' is a very solid, entertaining film showcasing the more grounded direction the MCU is heading as Tom Holland connects a web of past and present relationships to capture Peter Parker's depression and loneliness, supported by Jon Bernthal and Sadie Sink; while the action is fun and the humor definitely lands, the film is held back by tacky cinematography/editing choices and its lack of originality as the story feels almost identical to 'Thunderbolts*'
